planting.note: Direct sow in late winter to early spring as soon as soil can be worked; Witkiem Manita is bred specifically to be the earliest spring-sown broad bean available.

directions: Direct sow as soon as soil can be worked in late winter to early spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Witkiem Manita is a Dutch-bred fava bean known as the earliest spring-sowing broad bean on the market, reaching maturity in just 75-85 days on compact 18-inch plants. Short, well-filled pods hold about five white, high-tannin seeds with a notably strong, flavorful character prized over milder modern fava types. Harvest young for fresh eating or let pods fill out fully for freezing; its compact habit means less staking than taller fava cultivars.

planting.note: Direct sow in early spring (or fall in mild-winter climates) into fertile soil in full sun; Red Epicure grows tall and needs staking to support the heavy pod load.

directions: Direct sow into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, staking the tall 5-foot plants to support the pod load; Red Epicure is a rare English heirloom fava bean with distinctive chestnut-red seeds, often described as carrying a genuine chestnut-like flavor unusual among fava types. Shell beans dry to a deep burgundy color but keep their bright red hue if steamed rather than boiled. In mild-winter climates it can be fall-sown to overwinter for an earlier spring crop, since the plants tolerate frost well as seedlings.

planting.note: Direct sow February through May, or in fall (October-November) in mild-winter climates for overwintering; Bunyard's Exhibition is a heavy-cropping 1884 English heirloom.

directions: Direct sow into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Bunyard's Exhibition is a heavy-cropping English heirloom broad bean dating to 1884, producing long pods holding 8-9 white seeds on vigorous 54-inch plants. It can be sown in late winter through spring for a summer crop, or in fall in mild-winter climates to overwinter and crop earlier the following year. Its classic, robust fava flavor holds up well whether eaten fresh or frozen, and the heavy pod set makes it a dependable choice for a dedicated fava-bean bed.

planting.note: Direct sow in early spring, or fall in mild-winter climates; Jubilee Hysor is an early-maturing improved Windsor-type fava bean.

directions: Direct sow into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Jubilee Hysor is an improved Windsor-type fava bean among the earliest to crop from a spring sowing, producing well-filled pods with 6-8 seeds on tall, vigorous plants. It can also be sown in fall where winters are mild enough for the seedlings to overwinter. Its robust, old-fashioned broad bean flavor holds up even as the beans size up, making it forgiving of a slightly later harvest than some modern fava cultivars bred for a narrow picking window.

planting.note: Direct sow in late winter to early spring into well-drained soil in full sun; Pardina is a Spanish regional lentil type from the Tierra de Campos area.

directions: Direct sow into well-drained soil in full sun; Pardina is a small, brownish-grey Spanish lentil from the Tierra de Campos DOP region, grown on a thin-stalked, branching plant typical of lentils. It holds its shape well when cooked, unlike some softer lentil types, making it well suited to the classic Spanish lentejas stew and other slow-cooked dishes. Like other lentils it is drought-tolerant once established and fixes its own nitrogen, making it a low-input addition to a home vegetable garden.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost into well-drained soil in full sun; Pico Pardal is a Spanish heirloom known as the 'sparrow-beak' chickpea for its distinctively pointed seed shape.

directions: Direct sow into well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed; Pico Pardal is a small-seeded chickpea from León, Spain, named 'sparrow-beak' for the pronounced pointed beak on each seed. It carries a creamy, thin-skinned texture that cooks quickly compared to larger chickpea types, and is a traditional ingredient in the regional cocido maragato stew. Like other chickpeas it tolerates heat and drought well once established and needs minimal supplemental water through a hot summer.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost into well-drained soil in full sun, avoiding heavy or limy ground; Blanco Lechoso is a large-seeded Andalusian chickpea prized for its buttery texture.

directions: Direct sow into well-drained soil in full sun, avoiding heavy or limy ground, after frost danger has passed; Blanco Lechoso is a large, milky-white Andalusian chickpea with a very thin skin and buttery texture, considered excellent for hummus, purees, and stews where a smooth finished texture matters. It needs the same warm-season, drought-tolerant culture as other chickpeas, maturing in 100-120 days. Harvest when pods dry and rattle on the plant, then thresh and store the dried seeds for year-round use.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost into well-drained soil in full sun; Castellano is the classic chickpea of Castile and León, traditionally used in Spanish cocido stew.

directions: Direct sow into well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed; Castellano is a medium-to-large, light cream chickpea with a semi-wrinkled skin and a distinctive curved beak, originating in the Castile and León region of Spain. It is the traditional chickpea used in the classic cocido stew, prized for holding its shape and texture through long simmering. Grow it with the same warm-season, drought-tolerant culture as other chickpeas, harvesting dried pods once they rattle on the plant.

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed following last frost; Garrofón is a vining lima bean type and needs a trellis or other support to climb.

directions: Direct sow into warm, fertile soil in full sun alongside a trellis or other support for the vigorous climbing vines; Garrofón is the Valencian lima bean essential to authentic paella valenciana, producing flattened wide pods with large speckled or white seeds depending on the strain. Pick fresh at 3-4 months for the classic paella ingredient, or leave pods to dry fully on the vine past that point for storage beans. It is frost-tender like other lima beans and needs a full warm season to mature a complete crop.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 2-3 weeks before last frost; transplant into warm soil after all frost danger has passed. Hami needs a long, hot growing season to develop full sweetness.

directions: Transplant into warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger has passed; Hami melon is a famous Chinese melon from the Xinjiang region, producing oval fruit with crisp, aromatic orange-white flesh that is prized more for its satisfying crunch and sweetness than for strong aroma. It needs a long, hot growing season, 85-100 days, to fully develop its characteristic sugar content, making it best suited to regions with reliably hot, dry summers. Harvest when the fruit develops a full aroma and the skin color deepens, then eat fresh chilled as is traditional.

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed following last frost into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Violina needs a full warm season and ample vine space to mature its large fruit.

directions: Direct sow into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Violina is a Southern Italian heirloom butternut squash, its elongated, violin-shaped fruit (3-4 kg) covered in wrinkled, creamy-tan skin over dense, deep-orange, sweet flesh. It stores exceptionally well into winter, and its intense flavor and texture make it especially prized for risotto, gnocchi, and roasting in Italian cooking. Give the vigorous vines ample room to spread, and harvest once the rind hardens fully and resists thumbnail pressure, curing fruit in a warm, dry spot for a week before storage.
